current.text: He is healthy now after last season's hamstring injury.
LeBron James left the Lakers for the Sixers. Dončić and Austin Reaves are the remaining core, and the team is fully his.
Experts expect the highest usage in the league, about 38 to 41%, with around 36 minutes. They do not expect his usage to drop now that LeBron is gone.
His scoring should stay close to last season's league-leading level. Without LeBron, his assists could rise to about nine.
Experts rank him third overall and tier 1 at guard. Take him at pick 3 or 4, never at pick 2. One expert says Yahoo's rank of 3 is about right.
In an expert 9-cat mock draft he went at pick 4, after Jokic, Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.
If he keeps his late-season steals pace, he is a top 2 candidate.
Experts rank him over Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in 9-cat because of more usage, assists and rebounds. Shai keeps the edge in efficiency.
In an expert auction mock he went for 61 USD.
Josh would pay up to 64 USD and calls 61 USD a bargain, one of the best values of that draft.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league.
The heavy back-to-back load could bring his soft tissue injuries back. Experts call health the only concern with him, and say his health makes the Lakers more vulnerable than the top five West teams.
With a March 28 end, the Lakers play 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks, with 4 games in the week starting March 15. That is in the bottom half of the league.
Andy predicts 50 wins and a top six finish in the West for the Lakers.
The Lakers roster has two high-end players, Kessler, and many role players, so the shots and touches go mostly to Dončić and Reaves.

durable.text: His category profile is elite. Points, threes, assists and steals are all league outliers. His rebounds are far above other guards.
Getting both rebounds and assists is a rare combination that adds to his value.
He commits many turnovers, a league outlier on the weak side.
He is not a bad free throw shooter, but you cannot count on him for a good FT%. His FG% is only average, which is risky on his volume. Blocks and the two percentages are his weakest categories.
He is a high-usage player who is involved in almost every possession.
He reads passing lanes well, which gets him steals. He also draws a lot of charges.
On defense he does better against bigger players and often guards power forwards.
He has a history of soft tissue injuries: a calf injury, then a hamstring injury last season that cost him the playoffs.
Soft tissue injuries are the main risk to his value.

note: He is a top 3 player who covers four categories as league outliers: points, threes, assists and steals. He fits a punt TO build best, because about 3.9 turnovers per game is his only flagged weak spot. Both sites value him near 59 to 63 USD and an expert mock paid 61 USD, but Yahoo and ESPN average cost is 73.1 USD and our league paid 76 USD last season, so expect to pay above value to get him at pick 3 or 4. Early in the season, watch his calf and hamstring through the Lakers' heavy back-to-back schedule. Also watch his FG% on 22 shots a game, since experts call it only average.
